review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset labels 1.0 and 0.5 count as INCLUDE; 0.0 counts as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: Not a randomised controlled trial; observational study of complications following induced abortions. Does not compare surgical methods in a randomised design.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised controlled trial comparing conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) with manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for early first-trimester abortion. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT comparing two surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: Not an RCT; this is an epidemiological trends analysis comparing mortality and morbidity before and after Roe v Wade. No random allocation or comparison of surgical methods.

This is a randomised trial, but it compares a prostaglandin vaginal suppository versus placebo for cervical preparation prior to vacuum aspiration. It does not compare different surgical methods; the surgical procedure is the same in both arms. Therefore not eligible according to the selection criteria.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised controlled trial comparing dilatation and curettage (D&C) vs vacuum aspiration for first-trimester abortion. Meets all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration versus electric vacuum aspiration for first-trimester elective abortion. Compares two surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: RCT randomly assigning women to manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) or electric vacuum aspiration (EVA) for first-trimester abortion. Compares two distinct surgical approaches.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: Not an RCT; the study describes 47 women who underwent either vacuum aspiration or classical D&C, but no random assignment is mentioned. Appears to be a non-randomised comparative study.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised trial, but it compares two types of cannulae (metal vs flexible plastic) used within vacuum aspiration. The intervention is a variation of the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration), not a comparison of different surgical methods as specified in the selection criteria (e.g., D&C vs VA, MVA vs EVA). Therefore excluded.

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised trial comparing electric vacuum curettage versus manual vacuum aspirator for first-trimester abortion. Directly compares two surgical techniques.
